answer: Give every identity one append-only chain of signed actions, each link hashing the last, so its history rises like a mesa, layer by layer, and cannot be rearranged without breaking the signature. A clone copying it must fork it: two conflicting successors are a public warning, and both branches lose standing. A raven-like watcher reporting forks, and a violet checkpoint seal, make a rewritten past visible. Fresh chains carry no history, so mass cloning buys no trusted weight, only empty chains. The limit is key loss, which needs a slow verified recovery, not an instant reset.
